notes: Access: tier-1 HTTP only, no block encountered. Same headless WordPress 'trouble' REST backend used as evidence source (see bs156.json notes for architecture). Checked exhaustively: (1) trouble/taxonomy - the full ~175-term product taxonomy dump backing the frontend's '/products?type=<slug>' filter; scanned every term name for Clearance/Outlet/Final Sale/Last Chance/End of Line/Discontinued/Sale/Discount/Offer/Promo/Deal - none exist anywhere. (2) trouble/routes - the site's full 628-URL prerender/route manifest; none of /sale, /outlet, /clearance, /final-sale, /last-chance is a registered route (checked via exact match and via a broad keyword regex across all 628 routes: best|top-sell|popular|favourite|trend|sale|outlet|clearance|discount|offer|promo|deal - the only hit was a false positive, 'kristoffer' containing the substring 'offer'). (3) trouble/frontpage (homepage ACF modules) - no clearance/outlet/sale section or link anywhere in the promo/list/layout modules. (4) Per assignment hint, checked the 'Professionals' B2B/trade page (possible trade-login gate on merchandising pages, seen on other Danish design brands): it is public, not password-protected, and links to no sale/outlet catalogue - no trade gate found. Candidate URLs https://www.andtradition.com/sale, /outlet, /clearance all return HTTP 200 but render the generic '&Tradition' shell <title> (not '&Tradition — Products', which every genuine /products?type=X listing carries) and are absent from the 628-route manifest - i.e. unmatched/fallback routes rendering no real content, not genuine pages. Site's own search API returns an identical default result for every query tested (including 'sale', 'outlet', 'clearance', 'sample sale') - a known false-absence trap, not relied upon; taxonomy + route-manifest enumeration were used instead as the authoritative absence proof. No page anywhere on the site is merchandised by the site's own taxonomy as Clearance/Outlet/Final Sale/Last Chance/End of Line, and no generic temporary promotional 'Sale' page exists either (so the Sale-vs-Clearance ambiguity rule did not come into play - there was nothing borderline to flag). Conclusion: no genuine Clearance-type merchandising PLP exists on this site.
